rv.q: But “Lowcountry” is about shorthand personality traits rather than actual humans — the characters say and do dumbfounding things just to keep the show going.
It boldly tests the American theater’s much-advertised capacity for empathy while muddying our cherished moral clarity.
The play, while a bit undisciplined, has true firecracker wit.

The timing and execution of the diegetic song represents the balance of dark comedy and thriller suspense in Lowcountry, hampered by spurts of stagnancy but held together by naturalistic performances.
However, this talky play doesn’t get where it is going until the last ten minutes and has a great many unanswered questions that perplex as one watches the play.
But from the get-go “Lowcountry” was easily the most exasperating production I’ve sat through all year.
Lowcountry ambitiously takes on the least lovable and understandable members of our society and humanizes them.
What happens in 'Lowcountry' challenges the audience's understanding of moral ambiguity and situational ethics.
Balfour commands the audience’s attention, from how she sits in a chair to how she takes off her shoes and drinks wine.

cn.t: Rosebrock's dark thriller about a sex offender's first date draws mixed reviews for its ambitious moral complexity and firecracker wit, though critics fault heavy exposition and a talky script that only catches fire in its shocking final moments.

vr.q: Splendidly acted and directed, it paces its reveals with strong intentionality, making for somewhat of a slow burn that ultimately shocks and satisfies.
